_about: Lists for the generator tools: who lives where (people mix by region and terrain), the terrain words on place pages, encounter details, quick rolls, treasure and the no-repeat decks.

peopleMix._about: Multiplies each people's weight in peoples.json for NPCs rolled at a place. A place page can set its own with `peoples: {Merfolk: 3}`.

terrainWords._about: Words used in a place page's `terrain` list, and the travel terrain each one means.

streets.name: Streets
streets.about: Inside a town or city: alleys, rooftops, sewers and markets.

encounter._about: Encounter details. wants and tactics are by creature type (monsterType), with 'any' for all. situations and features are by travel terrain, with 'Streets' and 'any'. {monster} is the lead monster's name.

beast: Food. They are starving after a bad season and anything that moves is a meal.
Their young. A den or nest is close by and they will not let anyone near it.
Territory. The party has walked into ground they have marked and defended for years.
Water. The only drinkable water for miles is behind them.
To get away. They were driven here by something bigger and are panicking.
A carcass. They have a kill and will fight to keep it.
monstrosity: To feed, and the party smells like the easiest meal in the area.
To guard a spawn point thick with magic, which feeds them as they wait.
To lair. They are looking for a new den, and the party's camp would do.
Shiny things. Coins, cores and polished weapons draw them like a magpie.
To mate, and anything that comes near is a rival.
Revenge on whoever hurt them last, and the party smells like an adventurer.
undead: To finish something they started in life: a delivery, a guard post, a vow.
Warmth. They are drawn to living heat and cannot tell friend from food.
To be laid to rest, though they attack anyone who cannot do it.
To obey. Someone raised them and gave them an order they cannot break.
To keep the living out of a tomb, a battlefield or a ruin.
To spread. Each body they kill may rise to join them.
humanoid: Money. They are paid to stop anyone passing, and they would rather be paid without bleeding.
The party's gear, cores or coin.
Someone the party is travelling with, or someone they are looking for.
To keep a secret: a smuggling run, a hidden camp, a stolen cargo.
Food and shelter. They are desperate, not cruel.
Glory. They want to beat a team of adventurers and be talked about.
To prove themselves to someone watching.
To recruit. They will offer before they fight.
fiend: A bargain. They would rather trade than fight, and the price is always too high.
Souls, or at least suffering. They are here to enjoy themselves.
Something a cult promised them and has not delivered.
A way home. They were summoned and left behind.
To corrupt someone in the party, and they have picked who.
elemental: Nothing a mortal can understand. They are a piece of the weather that woke up.
To return to their element, and the party stands between them and it.
To grow. They feed on their element and the party is carrying some of it.
Release from a binding: a broken ward, a half-finished ritual.
aberration: Minds. They feed on thought and the party is thinking loudly.
To learn. They take people apart to see how they work.
A door. They are holding open a crack to somewhere else.
To be left alone, though they do not believe that anyone would leave them alone.
construct: To follow their last order, which nobody alive remembers giving.
To guard what they were built to guard.
Repairs. They are scavenging metal and cores to keep working.
A password the party does not know.
dragon: Treasure, and respect, in that order.
To be flattered. A clever party might talk its way past.
Territory. This valley, this coast, this sky is theirs.
To test the party. They are curious about adventurers.
fey: A game. They want to play, and the rules are theirs.
A name, a memory or a year of someone's life.
To punish a broken promise, whether or not the party made it.
giant: Tribute, as the old agreements say.
Food for the hold, and livestock first.
To settle a grudge with the nearest town.
A lost thing: a hammer, a child, a herd.
ooze: To dissolve whatever it touches. That is all.
Warmth and minerals. It is drawn to metal.
plant: To spread its seed, and bodies make good soil.
Sunlight. The party is standing in its light.
To protect the grove that grew it.
celestial: To judge. They have come to see whether someone here is worthy.
A message delivered, whatever it costs.
To stop a wrong that only they can see.
any: To be left alone. The party walked into them.
Whatever the party is carrying, which they can smell or sense.
To drive everyone off this ground before something happens here.
They are guarding a fresh spawn point thick with magic.

whyHere: A spawn point opened here in the last few days and the magic has not settled.
They followed a trail of blood, food or magic to this spot.
Someone left a gate open, a ward unrenewed or a cage unlocked.
This is where they always are. The locals know to avoid it, and the party didn't ask.
A storm, flood or fire pushed them out of their usual ground.
They are hunting the same thing the party is.
Someone sent them, and that someone is watching.
They were fleeing another team of adventurers and ran straight into this one.
The Adventure Society missed this nest in its last sweep.
The local magic is rising, and they came with it.
exits: Give them what they want, or something that smells like it: food, a shiny lure, a way past.
A show of force: one hard hit or a loud spell and they think twice. A DC {dc} Intimidation check makes them back off.
Back away slowly and leave them their ground. They don't follow past a landmark the DM picks.
Talk. Someone who speaks their language, or a DC {dc} Persuasion or Animal Handling check, buys a truce.
Distraction. Fire, noise or a thrown pack sends them after something else for a minute.
Hide. A DC {dc} group Stealth check and they pass by without noticing the party.
Bargain. They will trade passage for a favour, and they will remember it.
Point them at a better target: a rival, a nest, a bigger threat.
Outlast them. They tire, lose interest or the light changes and they leave.
Find the one in charge. Beat or persuade the leader and the rest go with it.

Road: An overturned cart for cover (half cover, difficult terrain around it).
A milestone shrine; touching it gives one creature advantage on its next save, once.
Deep ruts: a creature that dashes along them must make a DC 10 Dexterity save or fall prone.
A narrow bridge over a ditch, only wide enough for one at a time.
Dust kicked up by the fight: heavily obscured past 30 feet after the first round.
Farmland: A scarecrow that looks a lot like a person from a distance.
Tall crops: lightly obscured, and Stealth with advantage while you stay low.
An irrigation channel, 5 feet wide and 3 deep: difficult terrain.
A barn with a hayloft for high ground and a ladder to pull up.
Panicked livestock: at the top of each round, a random line of 20 feet is trampled (DC 12 Dexterity save or 1d6).
Delta and marsh: Reeds taller than a person: heavily obscured beyond 10 feet.
Sucking mud: difficult terrain, and a creature that ends its turn there is restrained until it uses an action to pull free (DC 12 Strength).
A half-sunk boat for cover and a dry place to stand.
Channels of deep water; heavy armour sinks.
Mist until noon: lightly obscured everywhere.
Forest: Thick undergrowth: difficult terrain off the path.
A fallen trunk for half cover, or three-quarters if you lie behind it.
Low branches: climbers get high ground and a +2 to ranged attacks down.
A ravine hidden by ferns (DC 13 Perception to spot before falling 10 feet).
Dim light under the canopy: lightly obscured.
Desert: Loose sand: difficult terrain on the slopes.
A rock outcrop, the only shade and the only high ground.
Heat shimmer: ranged attacks past 60 feet have disadvantage.
A sinkhole that opens on the third round under a random creature (DC 13 Dexterity save or fall 15 feet).
A dust devil crossing the field, blinding whoever it passes for a round.
Steppe: Open ground: nowhere to hide, and nothing to stop a charge.
Tall grass in one quarter of the field: lightly obscured.
A burrow field: difficult terrain, and a DC 10 Dexterity save on a dash or twist an ankle (speed halved for a minute).
A lone standing stone for half cover.
Wind strong enough to blow out torches and give disadvantage on ranged attacks into it.
Mountains: A narrow ledge: a creature shoved off falls 20 feet.
A cave mouth that the creatures know and the party doesn't.
Thin air above the snowline: a DC 10 Constitution save at the end of each round of hard fighting or gain a level of exhaustion.
Loose boulders that can be levered down a slope (Strength DC 14, 3d10 in a 10-foot line).
Jungle: Vines that grab: difficult terrain, and a creature that falls prone there is restrained until it uses an action to get free.
Canopy above: anything that climbs is hard to see (heavily obscured from below).
A river crossing with something already in the water.
Rain so heavy that ranged attacks past 30 feet have disadvantage.
Stinging plants that deal 1d4 poison to anyone shoved into them.
Coast: Wet rocks: a creature that dashes must make a DC 10 Dexterity save or fall prone.
The tide coming in: each round the dry ground shrinks by 5 feet.
A wreck on the sand for cover.
Sea caves that echo, so nobody can tell where a sound came from.
Surf that knocks over anyone standing in it (DC 12 Strength save each turn).
Open sea: A heaving deck: ranged attacks have disadvantage when the ship rolls (on a 1-2 on a d6 each round).
Rigging to climb for high ground, and to fall from.
A cargo hatch open below: a shove sends someone 10 feet into the hold.
Spray and wind: fires go out and loud voices don't carry.
The ship's own crew, frightened and in the way.
Streets: Market stalls to overturn, hide behind or climb.
A crowd that panics: difficult terrain, and area spells will hit bystanders.
Rooftops reached by a stack of crates (Athletics DC 10).
A narrow alley where only two can fight side by side.
The watch arriving in 1d4 + 2 rounds, and they will arrest everyone.
A sewer grate that opens onto a 10-foot drop into running water.
any: A choke point between two rocks or walls, only 5 feet wide.
High ground at one side of the field.
Something flammable: dry brush, a tar barrel, a pile of sacks.
Bad light: lightly obscured beyond 30 feet.

Road: The creatures are already fighting a merchant's guards when the party crests the hill.
A broken-down wagon blocks the road and the creatures are inside it.
They are waiting where the road narrows between two banks.
A patrol of the local lord's riders lies dead on the road; whatever did it is still here.
A traveller runs towards the party, shouting a warning a few seconds too late.
Farmland: The creatures are in a farmer's field and the farmer is begging someone to do something.
A herd has been scattered; the creatures are picking off the stragglers.
The fight starts in a barn and the hay catches fire.
Farmhands with pitchforks want to help and will mostly get in the way.
The creatures came up from a well that was sealed for good reason.
Delta and marsh: Fog or reeds limit sight to 30 feet.
The ground is unstable; a failed check drops someone into water.
A coin-farm patrol is overdue and these creatures are why.
The creatures are in the water, and the party is in a boat.
A green-stone barge is stuck on a mudbank and the crew are on the roof.
Forest: The trees have gone silent, and everyone knows what that means.
A hunter's trap has caught one of the creatures, and the rest are furious.
The creatures are dragging something heavy back to their den.
Woodcutters have fled and left their axes and fire behind.
Another team of adventurers is already here and wants the kill.
Desert: The party finds the creatures at the only waterhole for a day in every direction.
A sandstorm is an hour away and the fight has to be over before it hits.
The creatures are digging out something buried in the dunes.
A caravan's beasts have bolted and the creatures are between the party and the caravan.
Bones of the last group that tried this are scattered round the rocks.
Steppe: The creatures are running a herd down and the party is in the herd's way.
Riders from a clan camp watch from a ridge to see how the party fights.
A grass fire is coming and both sides know it.
The creatures are circling something wounded in the long grass.
There is nowhere to hide, so the creatures saw the party coming a mile off.
Mountains: The fight starts on a switchback, with a drop on one side.
The creatures are holding a pass, and there is no other way through.
An avalanche is a real risk if anyone uses loud magic.
A goat herder is stuck on a ledge above the creatures.
Snow begins to fall, thick and fast.
Jungle: The creatures are in the canopy; the party only sees leaves moving.
A temple ruin is half swallowed by roots, and the creatures nest inside.
A river is in flood and the only crossing is a fallen tree.
Insects are so thick that concentration checks are made with disadvantage.
Someone left trail markers that lead straight into the nest.
Coast: The creatures came out of the surf at low tide and will go back with the high.
A fishing village's boats are drawn up on the beach and the creatures are among them.
A wreck has washed in and the creatures are picking it over.
The party is on a sea cliff path when the creatures attack from above and below.
Smugglers' lights on the water: someone else is landing here tonight.
Open sea: The creatures come aboard over the rail at night.
The ship is becalmed and the creatures are circling.
A second ship is under attack and signalling for help.
Something has holed the hull and the hold is filling.
The crew wants to throw something overboard to buy their way out.
Streets: The creatures are loose in a market at the busiest hour.
The watch has already lost and wants the party to finish it.
The fight starts in a tavern and moves out into the street.
Someone in the crowd is helping the creatures.
A temple bell is ringing the alarm and people are running the wrong way.
any: The monsters are fighting each other when the party arrives.
A Normal-rank traveller is hiding nearby and needs rescue.
The monsters are unusually strong; the local magic is rising.
Someone is watching how the party fights and will want to talk after.

beast: They circle and look for the weakest, then all go for it at once.
The biggest one charges while the others flank.
They fight until hurt, then run and try again later.
monstrosity: It opens with its strongest attack on whoever looks most dangerous.
It uses the ground: high places, water, darkness.
It drags one victim away from the rest and fights there.
undead: They never retreat and never take cover.
They go for the living first and ignore anything that looks dead.
They mob the nearest creature and keep coming.
humanoid: Archers hang back behind cover while the rest hold the line.
They focus spellcasters first, because their leader told them to.
They try to take a hostage and bargain.
They use nets, caltrops and smoke before they use swords.
fiend: It talks the whole time, picking at whoever it can upset.
It sets the party against each other before it fights.
It holds back until someone is alone.
elemental: It goes straight for whatever matches its element: fire to dry wood, water to the river.
It ignores cover and fights in a straight line.
aberration: It attacks minds first and bodies after.
It has a way out that no one else can use.
It flees at the first real hit and comes back stronger.
construct: It keeps to its patrol until someone breaks a rule it was given.
It targets whoever touched what it guards.
dragon: It strafes with breath from the air and never lands near a fighter.
It fights from its lair's best ground and makes the party come to it.
fey: They play tricks first: illusions, charms, stolen boots.
They only fight for real if someone breaks their rules.
giant: It throws rocks until the party closes, then swings.
It grabs the smallest creature and uses it as a club or a shield.
any: They fight the nearest creature and switch to whoever hurts them most.
They try to push the party into the worst ground on the field.
The leader stays back while the rest wear the party down.

morale: When the leader falls, the rest flee.
At half their number, they break and run in every direction.
At half their hit points, each one tries to get away. Cornered, they fight harder.
When one of them dies, the rest stop to drag the body away.
They surrender when outnumbered, and offer to tell what they know.
They never break. Something is making them fight.
At half strength, the leader calls for help (see reinforcements).
At half strength, they fall back to better ground and try again.
When fire, water or bright light is used against them, they panic for a round.
They fight to the death to protect what they are guarding, and no further.
reinforcements: On round 3, another of the lead monster comes to the noise.
On round 4, 1d4 smaller creatures of the same kind arrive.
If the fight lasts more than 5 rounds, something bigger comes to see what's going on.
A rival group arrives on round 3 and attacks whoever looks weakest, party or monster.
The watch, a patrol or another team arrives on round 4, on the party's side.
No one else is coming. The party is on its own.

kinds.name: Stand-off
kinds.text: Both sides have seen each other and neither has moved. The first to act decides what this is.

kinds.name: Parley
kinds.text: They call out, or signal, before anyone attacks. They want to talk, and they want something.

kinds.name: Chase
kinds.text: They run as soon as they see the party. Catching them is the challenge, not killing them.

kinds.name: Passing by
kinds.text: They have somewhere to be and don't care about the party unless the party makes them care.

kinds.name: Aftermath
kinds.text: The fight already happened. The party finds the creatures wounded, or the bodies of whoever met them first.

kinds.name: Ambush being set
kinds.text: The party spots them before they spot the party, laying an ambush for someone else.

complications: The street ahead is closed: a cart has overturned and spilled live crabs everywhere.
A pickpocket tries the party, and a watchman saw it happen.
Someone mistakes one of the party for a person they owe money.
A festival procession blocks the way for an hour.
Rain turns the road to mud: travel takes twice as long today.
The person they came to see left this morning, and nobody will say where.
A rival team of adventurers has taken the same contract.
The price has doubled since yesterday, and the shopkeeper won't say why.
A child follows the party and won't leave.
The bridge toll has gone up, and the guard is new and nervous.
Someone has spread a rumour about the party, and people are staring.
A loose animal from an astral space is running through the crowd.
A noble's guard tells them to step aside and kneel.
The inn is full because of a wedding, and the wedding needs help.
A message for the party arrives, meant for someone else.
The local magic flares: low-rank spells misfire on a 1 on the d20 for the next hour.
An Adventure Society official wants to inspect their badges.
Their contact is drunk and very, very honest.
A thief stole the wrong bag and wants to give it back, for a fee.
A street preacher points at one of them and names a sin.
